title: Forty Days and Forty Nights
description: Forty Days and Forty Nights in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the six verses, and a piano.
about: George H. Smyttan’s Lenten hymn was published in 1856. The tune HEINLEIN was printed in Nuremberg in 1676 and is attributed to Martin Herbst.
underlay: For-ty days and for-ty nights Thou wast fast-ing in the wild; For-ty days and for-ty nights Tempt-ed, and yet un-de-filed.

lines: Thou wast fasting in the wild;
Stones Thy pillow; earth Thy bed.
Shall not we Thy sorrow share,
Glad with Thee to suffer pain?
Grant we may not faint nor fail.
So shall we have peace Divine;
Round us too shall Angels shine,
Keep, O keep us, Saviour dear,
That with Thee we may appear
